title: Canonical tree has depth zero when a term is fixed
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables and let $\rho$ be a restriction on those variables. If some term of $f$ is fixed by $\rho$ — that is, at least one conjunction of literals in $f$ has every literal fixed to true by $\rho$ — then the canonical decision tree of $f$ under $\rho$ has depth $0$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
ρ is a restriction on n variables
some term of f is fixed by ρ
replaced:
If some clause of $f$ is fixed (satisfied) by $\rho$, the canonical decision tree
for $f|_\rho$ is the leaf $\mathrm{true}$ and hence has depth $0$.
